name: Pharaoh (Pharaoh in Abram's time (Gen 12))
title: Ruler of Egypt during Abram's time
summary: This pharaoh was the ruler of Egypt when Abram and Sarai traveled there due to a famine in Canaan. He took Sarai into his harem after Abram presented her as his sister, but he was struck by God's plagues and sent them away once the truth was revealed. The event demonstrates God's protection of the patriarchal family and His promises to Abram.

keyEvents.title: Abram travels to Egypt due to famine
keyEvents.description: There was a famine in the land of Canaan, so Abram went down to Egypt to live there as a foreigner. This led him into contact with Pharaoh.

keyEvents.title: Abram presents Sarai as his sister
keyEvents.description: Abram asked Sarai to say she was his sister because he feared the Egyptians would kill him on account of her beauty. This lie caused Pharaoh to take an interest in her.

keyEvents.title: Pharaoh takes Sarai into his house
keyEvents.description: The officials of Egypt praised Sarai's beauty to Pharaoh, and she was brought into Pharaoh's house. For her sake, Pharaoh treated Abram well and gave him sheep, cattle, donkeys, male and female servants, and camels.

keyEvents.title: God strikes Pharaoh with plagues
keyEvents.description: The Lord struck Pharaoh and his household with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram's wife. This demonstrated God's direct intervention to protect the covenant promises.

keyEvents.title: Pharaoh Confronts Abram
keyEvents.description: Pharaoh summoned Abram and rebuked him for lying about Sarai being his sister. He asked why Abram had not told the truth, so that he might have taken her as a wife.

keyEvents.title: Pharaoh Sends Abram Away from Egypt
keyEvents.description: Pharaoh ordered his men to escort Abram out of the country along with his wife and all that he owned. Abram left Egypt with great wealth.
